citations.title: Home Health Services
citations.requirement: Governing statute for home health agencies (HHAs) and nurse registries. Covers licensure, staffing, service agreements, RN supervision and homemaker/companion registration.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Companions and homemakers may not provide hands-on personal care. Home health aides provide hands-on personal care. The administrator definition is at s. 400.462(1), personal care at (27), nurse registry at (25).

citations.title: Home health agencies to be licensed; expiration of license; exemptions; unlawful acts; penalties
citations.requirement: A license is required to provide hands-on care. The license number must appear in advertising. Advertising services not on the license is unlicensed activity. Exemptions are in subsection (6).

citations.title: Application for license; fee
citations.requirement: Requires CPA-compiled 2-year projections and proof of $250,000 per claim malpractice and liability insurance. Non-skilled agencies are exempt from accreditation. Subsection (2) provides for the licensure survey.

citations.title: Staffing requirements; notifications; limitations on staffing services
citations.requirement: Sets administrator qualifications (subsection (1)). A director of nursing is required only for agencies providing skilled nursing (subsection (2)). No staffing ratios are set.

citations.title: Patients with Alzheimer's disease or other related disorders; staff training requirements; certain disclosures
citations.requirement: HHA staff must complete s. 430.5025 dementia training. An HHA that claims special Alzheimer's care must disclose the services that make it suitable (subsection (2)).

citations.title: Home health service agreements; treatment orders; patient assessment; plan of care; provision of services; orders not to resuscitate
citations.requirement: (1) A written agreement states the services, the rates for privately paid services and the payment sources. (3) The agency arranges RN supervisory visits to the home of a patient receiving aide services, per the patient's direction, approval and agreement to pay for the visits. (4) The patient has the right to be informed of and participate in care planning and to receive a copy of the plan on request. (7) Personnel may withhold CPR on a valid DNR order (s. 401.45).

citations.title: Assistance with self-administration of medication and with other tasks
citations.requirement: Unlicensed assistance is allowed only for medically stable patients, with routine, regularly scheduled medications, upon a documented request and the patient's written informed consent. (3) lists permitted assistance, including keeping a record of each assist. (4) lists exclusions: injectables, tube administration, mixing or calculating doses, PRN meds requiring judgment, rectal/urethral/vaginal preparations, and others. (6) lists other tasks: glucometer, antiembolism stockings, oxygen cannula (no titration), CPAP (no titration), vital signs and colostomy bags.

citations.title: Licensure of nurse registries
citations.requirement: Referred CNAs, aides, companions and homemakers are independent contractors, and the registry may not supervise them. Used only for the nurse registry alternative.

citations.title: Registration of particular service providers exempt from licensure
citations.requirement: Homemaker and companion providers must register. The registration number must appear in ads (subsection (5)). Each worker's employment history must be verified (subsection (4)). Registration costs $50 per biennium (statutory, CPI-adjusted).

citations.title: Minimum licensure requirements
citations.requirement: (3) Report application and insurance changes to AHCA within 21 calendar days. (4) Give AHCA 30 days' notice before discontinuing operation, and notify clients. Arrange record custody, or publish notice weekly for 4 consecutive weeks. (5) On or before the first day of service, give each client the complaint, abuse hotline and Medicaid fraud hotline notices. Each licensee must have a written policy for giving these notices. (6) Proof of legal right to occupy. (14) Affidavit of compliance with s. 408.051(3) with the initial and renewal application.

citations.title: Background screening; prohibited offenses
citations.requirement: Level 2 screening of owners, administrators, financial officers and direct-care staff. Rescreen every 5 years.

citations.title: Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse
citations.requirement: Fingerprint results are shared through the Clearinghouse. Screening is renewed through it.

citations.title: Dementia-related staff training
citations.requirement: HHA, nurse registry and homemaker/companion staff: a 1-hour course within 30 days, and 2 additional hours within 7 months.

citations.title: Additional licensure requirements for home health agencies
citations.requirement: Startup, working-capital and contingency funds covering at least 3 months of projected expenses (contingency at least 1 month). A $500,000 surety bond if any controlling interest is a nonimmigrant alien (subsection (2)).

citations.title: Licensure Requirements
citations.requirement: (1) Application on AHCA Form 3110-1011 with the Addendum. (2)(a) Survey before initial licensure, then unannounced at least every 36.9 months. (4) Change of ownership: client records transfer to the new owner. (5) Satellite office in the same geographic service area, not separately licensed. (6) Satellite duties. (7) Drop-off sites. (8) Change of address, counties served, or office opening/closing: file Form 3110-1011 with zoning and right-to-occupy evidence. (9)(a) Administrator and DON or alternates are available to the public for any 8 consecutive hours between 7:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m., Monday-Friday. (9)(b) A staff person answers the phone and door and can reach the administrator. (9)(c) Surveyor access: the administrator or alternate is on premises within 1 hour of a surveyor's arrival, and a current patient list is produced within 2 hours. (9)(d) An agency with no skilled services must have written policies on RN supervisor availability during hours of patient service. (10) Return the license on closure.

citations.title: Personnel
citations.requirement: The 5/31/2026 version, read on flrules.org, controls. The Cornell page may show the prior version. (1) Administrator meets ss. 400.462(1) and 400.476(1) and designates a written on-site alternate. (1)(b) Notify AHCA of administrator changes; level 2 screening applies. (2)(i) No DON for an agency without skilled care. (3)(b) An RN may assign personal care tasks and keeps full responsibility. (3)(c) An RN provides supervisory visits, and the agency must have the client's written consent for the RN to enter the home. (3)(d) On-site supervision as needed, based on condition severity and aide training and experience, documented in the client file. (5)(b) A CNA needs current Florida certification, or a copy of another state's current certificate. (5)(c) Before an aide serves, the file must show 40 hours of training or a passed competency test. The 2026 text allows in-person, online or hybrid delivery, but the aide must demonstrate skills in person. (5)(c)15 requires 2 hours of medication-assistance training with a label-reading check. (5)(f)-(h) Limits on agency-taught aide courses; instruction by or under an RN with 2 years' experience, one in home health. (5)(i) Competency test AHCA 3110-1007 (Sept 2025): all 14 practical tasks and 90 of 104 written questions. (5)(k) Annual in-service each calendar year and current CPR. (5)(l)-(p) Aide duties and limits. (5)(m) RN review for medically stable patients. (5)(n) Patient informed and written consent for medication help. (5)(r) HIV/AIDS course within 30 days. (12) Homemaker and companion duties.

citations.title: Acceptance of Patients or Clients
citations.requirement: (1) Accept only when services can reasonably be provided safely in the home, including communication through a same-language staff person, interpreter or translation technology, and assure all assigned visits. (2) A written agreement is signed and dated by an agency representative and the client or representative; a copy is given to the client and the original kept in the file. (3) For aide, homemaker and companion clients without a treatment order, the agreement is the service provision plan (s. 400.491(2)) and is kept for one year after termination. (4) On termination, develop a plan and refer to another provider, and give written notice of the date and reason. This does not apply to private-pay clients who default on payment. Help clients assess eligibility for government programs if private funds are depleted.

citations.title: Plan of Care
citations.requirement: (3) The patient, caregiver or guardian must be told that they may be informed of the plan, participate in developing it, and have a copy on request. The remaining subsections cover plans developed with a physician or APRN and are triggered by skilled-care orders.

citations.title: Clinical Records
citations.requirement: (2) No disclosure without written consent of the patient or guardian; information is confidential and exempt from ch. 119. (3) Transfer a copy of the record to another agency on request. (4) Retain as required by s. 400.491; records must be retrievable during unannounced surveys. (5) Required record contents (referral source, assessment, ID sheet, plan, signed and dated service notes, supervisory visit notes, termination summary). (6) Signature rules: electronic signatures must be authenticated and dated, with safeguards against unauthorized access and a reconstruction process.

citations.title: Registration Requirements for Homemaker and Companion Services Providers
citations.requirement: (1) Register before providing services; licensed HHAs and nurse registries are exempt. (2) Renewal or change-of-ownership application at least 60 days before expiration. (3) AHCA Form 3110-1003, filed biennially. (6) The service area is the counties within the health service planning district of the address of record. (7) Diligent effort means two documented attempts to verify employment or contractual history. (8) A confidential client record is required, listing the contents named in the rule. (9) Accept only if services can be provided adequately and safely; supply capable staff for all visits.

citations.title: Emergency Management Plans
citations.requirement: (1) A written CEMP in the format of AHCA Form 3110-1022 (rev. 3/2013) per s. 400.492. (2) Forward electronically to the DOH-designated contact for approval. (3) Annual review. (4) Report changes in emergency-coordinator phone numbers to the county emergency management office and county health department. (6) Brief designated staff; keep a telephone contingency plan. (8) On admission, inform patients about the special needs registry (s. 252.355) and document in the file whether the patient will evacuate or stay home. (9) On imminent threat, contact patients needing ongoing services. (10) Procedures for patients who stay at home. (11) Notify patients if the agency ceases operation. (13)-(17) Special needs registry data, a prioritized patient list, and in-home medication and supply lists.

citations.title: Scope of Services
citations.requirement: (4) The license application must state explicitly which services are provided directly by employees and which by contract. The agency must provide at least one service directly to patients. (5) An agency contracting directly with an assisted living facility (ALF) or adult family care home resident coordinates with the facility and retains responsibility for its own services. (6) An agency in space within an ALF must notify AHCA in writing.

citations.title: Advance Directives
citations.requirement: Rule number and title confirmed from the Ch. 59A-8 rule list (eff. 7/11/2013). Rule text was not retrieved; pull it before writing this policy.

citations.title: Geographic Service Area
citations.requirement: Rule number and title confirmed from the rule list (eff. 7/8/2026). Rule text was not retrieved; pull the text for the service-area policy.

citations.title: Excellence in Home Health
citations.requirement: New rule listed with effective date 10/12/2026. Text was not retrieved; review it before publishing the manual.

citations.title: Mandatory reporting of abuse, neglect, or exploitation of vulnerable adults; mandatory reports of death
citations.requirement: Any person who knows or has reasonable cause to suspect that a vulnerable adult has been or is being abused, neglected or exploited must immediately report to the central abuse hotline. Subsection (2) covers reports of death. Seen in search results and the 2026 section header only; open the full text to confirm before finalizing.

citations.title: Clinical records
citations.requirement: Skilled-care clinical records, and a service provision plan for non-skilled clients, with a stated retention period after termination. Secondary sources show 6 years for skilled records and 3 years for non-skilled plans, but older versions said 1 year, and Rule 59A-8.020(3) says 1 year. Confirm current subsection text before finalizing.

citations.title: Right of inspection; violations; fines
citations.requirement: AHCA inspection authority and class-based fines. Section title confirmed from the 2025 Part III index; fine amounts were not verified.

citations.title: Screening of home health agency personnel; nurse registry personnel and contractors; and companions and homemakers
citations.requirement: Section title confirmed from the Part III index. Text was not retrieved; use with ss. 408.809 and 435.12 and confirm.

citations.title: Florida minimum wage and preemption
citations.requirement: Minimum wage is $15.00 per hour from 9/30/2026. Local governments may not set a higher private-sector minimum.

citations.title: Third party employment
citations.requirement: A third-party employer (agency) may not claim the FLSA companionship or live-in exemptions, so overtime applies.

citations.title: Electronic visit verification
citations.requirement: EVV is required for Medicaid personal care services (from 1/1/2020) and home health care services (from 1/1/2023).

citations.title: Workers' compensation definitions
citations.requirement: Workers' compensation coverage is mandatory for a non-construction employer with four or more employees.

citations.cite: iBudget Waiver Coverage and Limitations Handbook (July 2017)
citations.title: APD iBudget Personal Supports
citations.requirement: Personal Supports staff are 18+ with a high school diploma or GED and one year of verifiable experience (or 30 college semester hours). Providers keep training records for 5 years and complete the handbook's required training.

citations.title: State responsibilities (screening and enrollment of managed care network providers)
citations.requirement: Network providers serving SMMC plans must be screened and enrolled with Florida Medicaid.

citations.title: Provider reimbursement schedules and billing codes
citations.requirement: Medicaid fee schedules, including the 2026 Personal Care Services Fee Schedule. State-plan personal care covers recipients under 21 only (Rule 59G-4.215). SMMC LTC rates are negotiated with each plan.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Administrator Responsibilities (Non-Skilled Home Health Agency)
state_specifics: The administrator must meet s. 400.462(1) and s. 400.476(1), F.S. That means a Florida-licensed physician, PA or RN, or at least 1 year of supervisory or administrative experience in home health or a licensed facility.
No director of nursing is required while the agency provides no skilled nursing (s. 400.476(2); Rule 59A-8.0095(2)(i)). Hands-on care is delivered by home health aides and CNAs.
The application states which services are provided by employees and which by contract. The agency must provide at least one service directly (Rule 59A-8.003; Rule 59A-8.008(4)).
The administrator notifies AHCA of administrator changes, and the new administrator is level 2 screened (Rule 59A-8.0095(1)(b)).
No staffing ratios or caseload limits are set by statute or rule. The agency sets its own supervisory-visit and RN-hour standards.

policies.title: Alternate Administrator and Business-Hours Availability
state_specifics: Written designation of an on-site alternate administrator, who has responsibility and authority for daily operation during the administrator's absences.
The alternate meets s. 400.462(1) and s. 400.476(1) qualifications.
The administrator or alternate is available to the public for any 8 consecutive hours between 7:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m., Monday through Friday (Rule 59A-8.003(9)(a)).
A staff person answers the phone and door and can reach the administrator (Rule 59A-8.003(9)(b)).
Keep the office open during the hours listed on the license application.

policies.title: Licensure Track, Service Area, Advertising, Insurance and Financial Ability Requirements
state_specifics: Hands-on personal care requires a Home Health Agency license, which can be limited to non-skilled services, or a Nurse Registry license. Companion-only or homemaker-only care requires registration under s. 400.509.
Do not serve clients before the license or registration is issued. Advertising services not on the license is unlicensed activity (s. 400.464).
The license or registration number must appear in every ad, website and business card (s. 400.464; s. 400.509(5)).

The HHA keeps at least $250,000 per claim of malpractice and of liability insurance, and proves it at initial and renewal application (s. 400.471). The surety bond requirement for nonimmigrant-alien controlling interests is in s. 408.8065(2). Non-skilled agencies are exempt from accreditation.
Nurse-registry referrals are independent contractors the registry may not supervise (s. 400.506). This manual covers the employer model only.
Any advertised special Alzheimer's care must be accompanied by the disclosure required by s. 400.4785(2).

policies.title: Homemaker and Companion Services Registration and Geographic Service Area (companion-only service line)
state_specifics: Applies only if the agency offers companion-only or homemaker-only services under registration. A licensed HHA is exempt from registering (Rule 59A-8.025(1)).
The application states the specific geographic area (counties) to be served, within the health service planning district of the address of record (Rule 59A-8.025(6)).
A registrant holding a registration as of July 1, 2015 may keep serving the counties listed on it if a plan for supervising staff outside the primary service area is documented.
Register before providing services. File AHCA Form 3110-1003 biennially, and renew or file a change of ownership at least 60 days before expiration (Rule 59A-8.025(2)-(3)).
Registrants may not provide hands-on personal care.

policies.title: Satellite Offices and Drop-Off Sites (conditional)
state_specifics: Applies only if the agency opens a satellite office in the same geographic service area (Rule 59A-8.003(5)). Satellites are not separately licensed.

The policy covers: (a) professional staff coverage based on projected clients; (b) coordination of care and services; (c) supervision and service provision when staff are absent; (d) communication and integration between main and satellite offices; (e) access to patient records at the satellite.

It also covers: (f) monitoring of daily clinical and administrative activities, services, personnel and administrative issues; (g) periodic onsite visits by the administrator; (h) public availability of satellite hours if they differ from the main office.
Opening or closing an office, or changing address or counties served, requires AHCA Form 3110-1011 with zoning and right-to-occupy evidence (Rule 59A-8.003(8)).

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control (Agency Procedure and Client Care Policy Manuals)
state_specifics: The administrator maintains and adheres to the agency procedure and client care policy manuals. A DON does that only if skilled care is added (Rule 59A-8.0095(2)(a)4 and (2)(i)).
Review the manual annually and after any amendment to Ch. 59A-8, F.A.C. Rules 59A-8.003 and 59A-8.0095 were amended in 2026, so check the current text on flrules.org.
Keep a version log and an acknowledgment signature for each employee.
Keep a current manual available at the office for surveyors.

policies.title: Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement
state_specifics: Review a sample of active and closed clinical records at least quarterly, with documentation of each review.

Assure that: (1) the agency accepts only clients whose needs it can meet; (2) case assignment and management are appropriate and consistent with the plan, and plans are individualized; (3) services are coordinated and appropriate; (4) services and outcomes are complete, legible, dated and signed in the record.
Assure that: (5) agency policies are followed; (6) client data confidentiality is maintained.
Use QA findings to improve services (item 7), and document the corrective actions taken.

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
state_specifics: Medicaid network providers must be screened and enrolled with Florida Medicaid before contracting with SMMC LTC plans (42 CFR 438.602).
Bill only for verified, documented visits. SMMC LTC rates are negotiated with each plan, so keep each plan's rate in writing.
Give clients the Medicaid fraud hotline notice at the start of service (see CR-03).
Prohibit billing for services not on the license or registration.
Maintain a confidential internal reporting channel and a no-retaliation rule.

policies.title: Surveyor Access, Licensure Surveys and Certified Service Verification Reports
state_specifics: AHCA surveys before initial licensure, then unannounced at least every 36.9 months (Rule 59A-8.003(2)(a)).
The administrator or alternate is on premises within 1 hour of a surveyor's arrival. A current patient list is produced within 2 hours (Rule 59A-8.003(9)(c)).
The agency can verify that personal care services were provided. It produces a certified report of services by a named direct-service or contracted staff person for a specified period.
That report is due within 2 hours of the request, or within 3 hours if the period requested exceeds one year (Rule 59A-8.0095(2)(d); s. 400.497(5), F.S.).
Records must be retrievable during unannounced surveys (Rule 59A-8.022(4)).

policies.title: Changes of Ownership, Address and Operations; Closure Notices
state_specifics: Report application and insurance changes to AHCA within 21 calendar days (s. 408.810(3)).
Give AHCA 30 days' notice before discontinuing operation and notify clients. Arrange record custody, or publish notice weekly for 4 consecutive weeks (s. 408.810(4)).
On a change of ownership, client records transfer to the new owner (Rule 59A-8.003(4)). Return the license to AHCA on closure (Rule 59A-8.003(10)).
Change of address, counties served, or office opening/closing: file Form 3110-1011 with zoning and right-to-occupy evidence (Rule 59A-8.003(8)).
A registrant files a renewal or change of ownership at least 60 days before expiration (Rule 59A-8.025(2)).

policies.title: Client Rights and Responsibilities
state_specifics: The client has the right to be informed of and participate in care planning and to receive a copy of the plan on request (s. 400.487(4); Rule 59A-8.0215(3)).
Give each client written rights and the required notices on or before the first day of service (s. 408.810(5)).
For Medicaid HCBS clients, honor the HCBS settings rule: choice, privacy, dignity and freedom from coercion.
Clients may refuse the RN supervisory visit. The RN may enter the home only with written consent (Rule 59A-8.0095(3)(c)).

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: Give every client the AHCA complaint notice on or before the first day of service (s. 408.810(5)).
Record, investigate and respond to each complaint in writing, and report outcomes through QA (GOV-07).
Never retaliate against a client or employee for filing a complaint.
For suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation, call the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873.

policies.title: Required Hotline and Complaint Notices at Start of Service
state_specifics: On or before the first day of service, give each client the complaint, abuse hotline and Medicaid fraud hotline notices (s. 408.810(5)).
Each licensee must have a written policy for giving these notices. This is that policy.
Abuse Hotline: 1-800-962-2873. Use the current AHCA-provided notice text and numbers for the complaint and Medicaid fraud lines.
Keep the signed notice acknowledgment in the client record.

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: No disclosure of client information without written consent of the client or guardian (Rule 59A-8.022(2)). Records are confidential and exempt from Ch. 119.
On request, transfer a copy of the record to another agency (Rule 59A-8.022(3)).
The homemaker/companion client record is also confidential (Rule 59A-8.025(8)).
Provide the HIPAA Notice of Privacy Practices, and train staff at hire and annually.

policies.title: Client Property, Gifts and Financial Exploitation Prevention
state_specifics: Aide training includes respect for the client's privacy and property (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(c) topic 8).
Prohibit caregivers from borrowing money, accepting gifts, becoming a beneficiary, or handling a client's cards or checks.
Any shopping or errand money is documented with receipts and a signed log.
Suspected exploitation of a vulnerable adult is reported to the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873 (see SAF-01).

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
state_specifics: Acceptance of a client requires the ability to communicate through a same-language staff person, an interpreter or translation technology (Rule 59A-8.020(1)).
Do not condition admission or treatment on advance-directive status (Rule 59A-8.0245(1)).
Provide aids and services for clients with disabilities at no charge.
Aide training covers cultural differences in families (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(c) topic 13).

policies.title: Service Agreement, Rates and Billing Disclosure
state_specifics: A written agreement at the start of services states the services, the rates for privately paid services and the sources of payment (s. 400.487(1)).
The agreement is signed and dated by an agency representative and the client or representative. The client gets a copy and the original goes in the file (Rule 59A-8.020(2)).

For homemaker, companion and aide clients without a practitioner's treatment order, the agreement serves as the service provision plan (s. 400.491(2)) and is kept for one year after services end (Rule 59A-8.020(3)).
State minimum shift lengths, cancellation terms and the RN supervisory-visit consent and payment terms in the agreement.

policies.title: Advance Directives and Do Not Resuscitate Orders
federal: 42 CFR 489.102 (not applicable unless Medicare-certified; included for reference only)
state_specifics: State the agency's position on Florida advance-directive law. Never condition treatment or admission on whether a directive was executed or waived. Conflicts are resolved under Ch. 765, F.S. (Rule 59A-8.0245(1)).

Before services begin, give each adult client a copy of 'Health Care Advance Directives – The Patients' Right to Decide' (AHCA, rev. April 2006) or an equivalent description of Florida law (Rule 59A-8.0245(2)(a)).
Before services begin, give each adult client written information about the agency's advance-directive policies (Rule 59A-8.0245(2)(b)).
The record documents whether a directive has been executed. A copy of any directive goes in the record. If no copy is received, document that one was requested (Rule 59A-8.0245(2)(c)).

CPR may be withheld or withdrawn only with a valid DNRO executed under s. 401.45, F.S. (Rule 59A-8.0245(3); s. 400.487(7)). Rule 59A-8.0245 text was not retrieved in research, so pull the rule before publishing.

policies.title: Scope of Services — What Home Health Aides and CNAs May and May Not Do
state_specifics: Aides and CNAs may do: (1) personal care in a written assignment by a licensed health professional; (2) maintaining a clean, safe environment; (3) other tasks taught by a licensed professional for a specific patient, limited to the rule's listed tasks.

They may also keep records of personal care activities, observe and report appearance and gross behavioral changes to the RN, and supervise self-administered medication within the four listed steps (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(l)).

Prohibited tasks are listed in Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(p), starting with therapeutic services requiring licensure. The research text was cut off partway through the list (at least 10 items). Copy the full list from the rule before publishing.
Also prohibited are injectables, tube administration, mixing or calculating doses, and PRN meds requiring judgment (s. 400.488(4)).
The license application states which services are provided directly versus by contract (Rule 59A-8.008(4)).

policies.title: Homemaker and Companion Duties and Limits (no hands-on care)
state_specifics: Companions and homemakers may not provide hands-on personal care (s. 400.462(8), (22)).
Homemaker duties are housekeeping, meal preparation, laundry, shopping and cosmetic assistance. Companion duties are company, escort and a written service record (Rule 59A-8.0095(12)).
Both may only verbally remind clients about medication.
Reassign to an aide or CNA, with an RN-supervised service plan, if the client needs hands-on help.

policies.title: Client Intake, Eligibility, Admission Criteria, Case Assignment and Assessment
state_specifics: Accept a client only if there is a reasonable expectation that services can be provided safely in the home. That includes same-language communication via staff, interpreter or translation technology (Rule 59A-8.020(1)).
Assure the client receives all assigned visits, and supply capable employees for the contracted services (Rule 59A-8.020(1); Rule 59A-8.025(9)).
Set and keep written criteria for admission, case assignment and case management, with records (Rule 59A-8.0095(2)(c)4).
Decline or refer clients whose needs exceed the non-skilled license, such as skilled nursing needs.
Record each client's disability basis, diet restrictions, allergies and activity limits at intake.

policies.title: Service Plan (Service Provision Plan) and Plan Updates
state_specifics: Where no treatment order exists, the signed written agreement is the service provision plan (Rule 59A-8.020(3); s. 400.491(2)).
Tell the client, caregiver or guardian that they may be informed of the plan, participate in developing it, and have a copy on request (Rule 59A-8.0215(3); s. 400.487(4)).
The RN reviews the plan at supervisory visits and when the client's condition changes.
Keep individualized aide assignment sheets reflecting the plan.

policies.title: Delegation and RN Assignment of Personal Care Tasks
state_specifics: An RN may assign personal care tasks to LPNs, CNAs and home health aides, and keeps full responsibility for those tasks (Rule 59A-8.0095(3)(b)).
The RN ensures each aide or CNA is qualified for each assignment based on training and experience.
Adopt written delegation procedures for nursing tasks and activities as specified in Ch. 64B9-14, F.A.C. (Rule 59A-8.0095(2)(c)5).
Document assignments in the client file.

policies.title: Supervision of Caregivers and RN Supervisory Visits
state_specifics: The agency arranges RN supervisory visits to the home of a client receiving aide services, per the client's direction, approval and agreement to pay (s. 400.487(3)).
Obtain written consent from the client or guardian for the RN to enter the home (Rule 59A-8.0095(3)(c)).

The RN provides on-site supervision as needed, based on the severity of the client's condition and the aide's or CNA's training and experience. The rule sets no fixed frequency (Rule 59A-8.0095(3)(d)).
Document every supervisory visit in the client file.
Supervisory-visit notes are part of the required client record (Rule 59A-8.022(5)).

policies.title: Availability of the RN Supervisor During Hours of Client Service
state_specifics: An agency with no skilled services must have written policies on the availability of a registered nurse supervisor during hours of client service (Rule 59A-8.003(9)(d)).
Name the RN supervisor and a backup, and publish a phone number that aides and clients can reach during all service hours.
Aides report changes in condition to the RN supervisor, and the RN returns calls within the agency's stated time.
Log RN contacts and keep a schedule of RN coverage by service hours.

policies.title: Medication Assistance and Self-Administration Support
state_specifics: Assistance is allowed only for medically stable clients with routine, regularly scheduled medications, on a documented request and the client's written informed consent (s. 400.488).

An RN reviews and reconciles all prescribed and over-the-counter medications to confirm the client is medically stable (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(m)). A licensed health care professional informs the client or caregiver and obtains written consent under s. 400.488(2) (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(n)).

Aides need 2 hours of medication-assistance training, including a check that they can read the prescription label (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(c)15). Permitted aide actions are in (5)(o)1-4. Keep a record of each assist (s. 400.488(3)).
Excluded: injectables, tube administration, mixing or calculating doses, PRN medications requiring judgment, and rectal, urethral or vaginal preparations (s. 400.488(4)).
Other permitted tasks: glucometer, antiembolism stockings, oxygen cannula and CPAP (no titration), vital signs and colostomy bags (s. 400.488(6)).

policies.title: Scheduling, Missed Visits and Continuity of Care
state_specifics: Assure the client receives all assigned visits (Rule 59A-8.020(1); Rule 59A-8.025(9)).
Name a backup caregiver for each case, and notify the client and the RN supervisor promptly when a visit will be missed.
Log every missed visit, the reason and the make-up plan, and review them in QA.
Travel between clients is paid work time (29 CFR 785; DOL direct care guidance).

policies.title: Electronic Visit Verification and Timekeeping
state_specifics: EVV is required for Medicaid personal care services (from 1/1/2020) and home health care services (from 1/1/2023).
Use the EVV system each SMMC LTC plan or APD requires, and reconcile EVV records to payroll and billing.
Record actual start and stop times, and correct them with a documented reason.
Agencies may not claim the FLSA companionship exemption, so record all hours for overtime (29 CFR 552.109).

policies.title: Change in Client Condition and Emergencies in the Home
state_specifics: Aides observe and report appearance and gross behavioral changes to the RN (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(l)5).
Aide training covers recognition of emergencies and follow-up (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(c) topic 7). Call 911 first in a life-threatening emergency.
CPR may be withheld only with a valid DNRO under s. 401.45 (s. 400.487(7)). Aides and CNAs keep current CPR (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(k)).
Notify the RN supervisor, emergency contact and physician, and complete an incident report (SAF-02).

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Termination of Services
state_specifics: For clients needing continuing care, develop a plan and refer to another agency or provider before termination (Rule 59A-8.020(4)).
Give written notice of the termination date, the reason and the plan for continued services. This does not apply to private-pay clients who default on payment.
Provide help assessing eligibility for government-funded programs if private funds are depleted.
Place a copy of the written termination notice in the record (Rule 59A-8.025(8)(h) for registrants).
Include a termination summary in the client record (Rule 59A-8.022(5)).

policies.title: Coordination with Medicaid Programs and Payers (SMMC LTC, APD iBudget, Area Agencies on Aging)
state_specifics: Enroll as a Florida Medicaid provider, then credential with each SMMC LTC plan in the service region (42 CFR 438.602).
State-plan personal care (S9122) covers recipients under 21 only (Rule 59G-4.215). Adult LTC rates are negotiated with each plan.
APD iBudget Personal Supports staff are 18+ with a high school diploma or GED and 1 year of verifiable experience. Keep training records for 5 years.
Follow each plan's or AAA's authorization, billing, EVV and reporting requirements.
Retain each payer's service authorization in the client record.

policies.title: Skilled Services Not Provided — Requirements That Apply If Skilled Services or LPNs Are Added
state_specifics: The agency does not provide skilled nursing. Adding it requires an 'Addition of Skilled Care Services' application, accreditation within 120 days, a DON and a 24-hour on-call system.

If skilled services are added, the agency needs written policies for 24-hour availability to licensed professional nursing staff by active skilled clients, with an on-call system in which nursing staff can communicate directly with the client (Rule 59A-8.003(9)(d)).
The DON would maintain and adhere to the agency procedure and client care policy manuals (Rule 59A-8.0095(2)(a)4).
The DON, administrator or alternate would establish biomedical waste policies for agencies providing nursing and physical therapy services (Rule 59A-8.0095(2)(b)).
If LPNs are used, policies provide for annual evaluation of the LPN's performance by the RN (Rule 59A-8.0095(4)(a)).

policies.title: Services to Residents of Assisted Living Facilities and Adult Family Care Homes; Contracted Staff
state_specifics: An agency contracting directly with an ALF or adult family care home resident coordinates with the facility and keeps responsibility for its own services (Rule 59A-8.008(5)).
An agency in space within an ALF must notify AHCA in writing (Rule 59A-8.008(6)).
Find out and document the facility's evacuation plan for each resident (Rule 59A-8.027(8)).
State in the license application which services are by contract versus employee (Rule 59A-8.008(4)).

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Florida Abuse Hotline: 1-800-962-2873. Staff who know or suspect abuse, neglect or exploitation of a vulnerable adult report immediately to the hotline.
Post the hotline number in the office, and give it to every client (s. 408.810(5)).
Level 2 screening and rescreening every 5 years (s. 408.809).
Train staff at orientation and annually on recognizing and reporting abuse.
Notify the administrator after reporting. Never retaliate against a reporter.

policies.title: Incident Reporting
state_specifics: Staff report any incident (fall, injury, medication assistance error, property damage, allegation of abuse) to the RN supervisor and administrator the same day.
Complete a written incident report and file it in the client record and QA file.
Report to the Abuse Hotline (1-800-962-2873) when abuse, neglect or exploitation is suspected.
Review incident trends quarterly in QA (GOV-07).
Report deaths and changes required by AHCA through the channels in REC-03.

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Policies are consistent with recommended CDC and OSHA guidelines for safety, universal precautions and infection control (Rule 59A-8.0095(2)(c)1).
Aide training includes basic infection control (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(c) topic 4).
Provide PPE and OSHA bloodborne pathogen training where occupational exposure exists.
Document exposure incidents and follow-up.

policies.title: Biomedical Waste and Sharps Handling
state_specifics: Biomedical waste policies are required for agencies providing nursing and physical therapy services (Rule 59A-8.0095(2)(b)). They are adopted here so they are in place if skilled services are added.
Aides do not handle sharps or injectables (s. 400.488(4)).
Clients' own sharps are not disposed of by caregivers. Notify the RN.
Contaminated disposable items from personal care are bagged and disposed of per CDC/OSHA guidance.

policies.title: Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan: Development, Approval, Annual Review and Contact Updates
state_specifics: Maintain a written CEMP in the format of AHCA Form 3110-1022 (rev. 3/2013), per s. 400.492 (Rule 59A-8.027(1)).
Forward the completed plan electronically to the Department of Health contact for approval, and review it annually, making substantive changes (Rule 59A-8.027(2)-(3)).
Report changes in telephone numbers of emergency coordinators, including after-hours numbers, to the county Emergency Management office and county health department (Rule 59A-8.027(4)).
A new owner reviews the plan after a change of ownership (Rule 59A-8.027(5)).
Renewal applications need a CEMP approval letter or proof of submission within the last 365 days.

policies.title: Emergency Staffing, Communication Contingency, Continuity of Care and Cessation of Operations
state_specifics: In an emergency, inform all staff designated for emergency measures of their duties (Rule 59A-8.027(6)(a)).
Keep a communication contingency plan if phones are down, such as cell phones, ham radio, public announcements, driving to the home, or contacting police or rescue (Rule 59A-8.027(6)(b)).
On imminent threat, contact clients needing ongoing services, and the ALFs and adult family care homes served, to confirm each client's plan (Rule 59A-8.027(9)).
Before an emergency, establish how far the agency will continue care during and after it. Determine which clients staying home need care, and designate staff (Rule 59A-8.027(10)).

If the agency ceases operation, inform clients and facilities, arrange for essential services, and report status to the local emergency operations center. Document efforts when special needs clients cannot be served (Rule 59A-8.027(11)-(12)).

policies.title: Client Emergency Preparedness at Admission, Special Needs Registry and In-Home Medication Lists
state_specifics: At admission, inform clients and caregivers of the county special needs registry (s. 252.355). Document in the file whether the client will evacuate or stay, whether a caregiver can take over, and whether the agency must continue services (Rule 59A-8.027(8)).
Collect registration information for special needs clients who need continuing care and submit it to the county Emergency Management office (Rule 59A-8.027(13)).
Tell registered clients that special needs shelters are a last-resort option and services may not equal those at home (Rule 59A-8.027(14)).
Keep a current prioritized client list with the s. 400.492(2) information, and furnish it to the county health department and Emergency Management office on request (Rule 59A-8.027(15)).

Each special needs client's record includes the s. 400.492(1) information. Keep a list of medications, supplies and equipment (names, dose, frequency, route, time, allergies, physician, pharmacy) in the client's home (Rule 59A-8.027(16)-(17)).

policies.title: Caregiver Safety in the Home and Workplace Violence
state_specifics: Workers' compensation is mandatory at 4 or more employees, including part-time (s. 440.02).
Aide training covers maintaining a clean and safe environment and safe transfer techniques (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(c)).
Staff may leave an unsafe home and call the RN supervisor or administrator. Document the event.
Provide an after-hours contact for caregivers.

policies.title: Transporting Clients
state_specifics: Transport clients only with written authorization in the service agreement, and with a licensed, insured driver.
Check hired and non-owned auto coverage, and confirm a driver's license and driving record before authorizing.
Mileage reimbursement for work travel follows the IRS standard rate (72.5 cents per mile for 2026), unless the agency's own plan is stated.
Drivers use child and mobility safety restraints as applicable.

policies.title: Caregiver Qualifications, Registry and Certification (CNAs and Home Health Aides)
state_specifics: Before a CNA works, document current Florida CNA certification, or a copy of another state's current certificate (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(b)).
Before a home health aide works, document at least 40 hours of training or a passed competency test (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(c)).

The 40-hour training covers 16 subjects: communication; observation and reporting; temperature, pulse and respiration; infection control; basic body functions to report; clean and safe environment; emergencies; client characteristics, privacy and property; hygiene and grooming.

It also covers: transfers and ambulation; range of motion and positioning; nutrition and fluids; cultural differences; food preparation and chores; self-administered medication (min. 2 hours, including label reading); other pertinent topics.
The file shows the training or test before the aide serves any client.

policies.title: Home Health Aide Training Program, Competency Testing and Instructor Qualifications
state_specifics: Aide training is performed by, or under the general supervision of, an RN with at least 2 years of nursing experience, one in home health care (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(h)).
Alternatively, administer the Home Health Aide Competency Test (AHCA 3110-1007) and keep documentation of the passing result (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(i)).
The test requires all 14 practical tasks and 90 of 104 written questions. An RN, or an LPN under RN supervision, administers and evaluates the practical portion.
The 2026 text allows in-person, online or hybrid delivery, but the aide must demonstrate skills in person.

policies.title: Background Checks and Employee Registries
state_specifics: Level 2 fingerprint screening through the Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse for owners, the administrator, the financial officer and every client-contact employee, before client contact (ss. 408.809, 435.12).
Rescreen every 5 years. Clearinghouse help: 850-412-4503.
Verify each worker's employment history, with two documented attempts (diligent effort) to verify it (s. 400.509(4); Rule 59A-8.025(7)).
Do not assign anyone with a disqualifying offense to client contact, and check the Clearinghouse for results.

policies.title: Orientation, Competency Evaluation and Annual In-Service Training
state_specifics: Aides and CNAs receive in-service training each calendar year and keep current CPR from an approved provider such as the American Red Cross or American Heart Association (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(k)).
Complete the 2-hour medication-assistance training before an aide assists with medications (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(c)15).
Orientation covers agency policies, abuse reporting, infection control, emergency procedures and client rights.
Document attendance, topics and hours for each employee.

policies.title: Dementia-Related and HIV/AIDS Staff Training
state_specifics: Dementia training under s. 430.5025: basic information at hire, a 1-hour course within 30 days for staff with client contact, and 2 additional hours within 7 months for HHA and companion/homemaker staff.
HHA staff must complete the s. 430.5025 training (s. 400.4785).
One-time HIV/AIDS course within 30 days of employment (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(r)).
Keep certificates in each personnel file.

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
state_specifics: The research did not retrieve a Florida rule prescribing TB test intervals. Set the screening schedule from the agency's infection-control policy and CDC/OSHA guidance (Rule 59A-8.0095(2)(c)1).
Screen at hire and after known exposure, and record results in the personnel file, kept apart from the general file.
Exclude staff with communicable illness from client contact until cleared.
Offer hepatitis B vaccination where OSHA requires.

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Each file shows CNA certificate or 40-hour training or competency test result, CPR, annual in-service, medication training, HIV/AIDS and dementia training.
Each file shows level 2 screening results and the employment-history verification attempts.
Keep the signed job description, orientation record and RN competency evaluation.
Keep aide training records for 5 years for APD iBudget services (iBudget Handbook).

policies.title: Wage, Hour and Overtime Compliance
state_specifics: Florida minimum wage is $15.00 per hour from 9/30/2026 ($14.00 from 9/30/2025). Local governments cannot set a higher private-sector minimum (s. 218.077).
Agencies may not claim the FLSA companionship or live-in exemptions, so overtime applies (29 CFR 552.109).
Travel between clients during the workday is paid time.
Workers' compensation is required at 4 or more employees, and part-time employees count (s. 440.02).
Track the next minimum-wage change and adjust pay and prices.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Aide training covers respect for the client, privacy and property (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(c) topic 8).
Prohibit gifts, loans, personal business with clients, social-media disclosure of client information and use of client property.
Staff report boundary concerns to the administrator.
Discipline for violations up to termination, and report suspected abuse or exploitation to the Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873.

policies.title: Client Records, Electronic Signatures and Retention
state_specifics: Record contents: referral source, assessment, identification sheet, plan, signed and dated service notes, supervisory visit notes and a termination summary (Rule 59A-8.022(5)).
Electronic signatures must be authenticated and dated, with safeguards against unauthorized access and a reconstruction process (Rule 59A-8.022(6)).

Retain as required by s. 400.491. The service provision plan is kept 1 year after termination under Rule 59A-8.020(3). The s. 400.491 text was not confirmed in research, so confirm the current retention period before publishing.
Records must be retrievable during unannounced surveys (Rule 59A-8.022(4)).
Keep offsite or cloud data stored in the continental U.S., its territories or Canada.

policies.title: Homemaker and Companion Confidential Client Record
state_specifics: Keep a confidential record for each client with: (a) full legal name, address, phone, age and the disability if it is the basis for service; (b) name and phone of emergency contact, next of kin or guardian, and physician.

Also: (c) copy of any contract or written service agreement; (d) services provided, with duration and frequency of visits; (e) dietary restrictions if the provider prepares, orders or accompanies the client to meals.
Also: (f) food allergies; (g) activity limitations pertaining to service delivery; (h) copy of any written termination notice.
The same record format may be used for aide clients, with the RN additions in REC-01.

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Report application and insurance changes to AHCA within 21 calendar days (s. 408.810(3)).
Report administrator changes and submit the change forms, with level 2 screening of new personnel (Rule 59A-8.0095(1)(b)).
Report patient count and CEMP approval or submission status on the renewal application. HHA licenses renew every 2 years.
Give AHCA 30 days' notice before discontinuing operation (s. 408.810(4)).
Report emergency coordinator phone changes to the county Emergency Management office and health department (Rule 59A-8.027(4)).

documents.form_number: Application: AHCA Form 3110-1011 (April 2019), plus the Health Care Licensing Application Addendum (rule 59A-35.060). The application form itself was not fetched or reviewed.

documents.how_used: Content requirements for the homemaker/companion-only registration path (client record, supervision plan, client-acceptance standard).

required_items.text: Written policies and procedures governing 24-hour availability to licensed professional nursing staff by active patients receiving skilled care. They must describe an on-call system in which designated nursing staff can communicate directly with the patient. (Skilled agencies only.)

A home health agency that does not provide skilled services shall have written policies and procedures that address the availability of a registered nurse supervisor during hours of patient service. (This applies to a non-skilled personal care agency.)

If the agency operates a satellite office, it must: (a) ensure coverage of professional staff based on projected clients; (b) coordinate care and services by staff; (c) ensure supervision and service provision when staff are absent; (d) maintain communication and integration of services between main and satellite offices; (e) provide access to patient records at the satellite office; (f) monitor daily clinical and administrative activities, services, personnel and administrative issues; (g) ensure periodic onsite visits by the administrator; (h) make the satellite office's hours available to the public if they differ from the main office. (Conditional on having a satellite office.)

Written designation of an on-site alternate administrator for the administrator's absences. This person has responsibility and authority for daily operation during those absences and must meet ss. 400.462(1) and 400.476(1), F.S.
The director of nursing must maintain and adhere to agency procedure and patient care policy manuals. (Not required for an agency that does not provide skilled care; see (2)(i).)

The director of nursing, administrator or alternate administrator shall establish policies and procedures on biomedical waste for agencies providing nursing and physical therapy services. (Applies only if those services are provided.)
Policies and procedures consistent with recommended CDC and OSHA guidelines for safety, universal precautions and infection control procedures.
Set or adopt policies for, and keep records of, criteria for admission to service, case assignments and case management.
Establish and adopt policies and procedures for the delegation process of nursing tasks and activities as specified in Chapter 64B9-14, F.A.C.

A process to verify that skilled nursing and personal care services were provided. The director of nursing must be able to produce a certified report of home health services provided by a named direct-service or contracted staff person for a specified period. The report is due to a surveyor within two hours of the request, or within three hours if the period requested is longer than one year.

An ongoing quality assurance program with at least quarterly documented review of a sample of active and closed clinical records. It must assure that: 1. the agency accepts patients whose service needs it can meet; 2. case assignment and management are appropriate, adequate and consistent with the plan of care, and plans of care are individualized; 3. nursing and other services are coordinated, appropriate, adequate and consistent with plans of care; 4. all services and outcomes are completely and legibly documented, dated and signed in the clinical record; 5. the agency's policies and procedures are followed; 6. confidentiality of patient data is maintained; 7. QA findings are used to improve services.

RN assignment of personal care tasks to LPNs, CNAs and home health aides. The RN maintains full responsibility for those tasks and must ensure the aide or CNA is qualified for each assignment based on training and experience.

RN supervisory visits of unlicensed assistive personnel under s. 400.487(3), F.S., with written consent from the patient or the patient's guardian or legal representative for the RN to enter the home. The RN provides on-site supervision as needed, based on the severity of the patient's condition and the aide's or CNA's training and experience. Supervisory visits are documented in patient files.
Provision in agency policies and procedures for annual evaluation of the LPN's performance of duties by the registered nurse. (Applies if LPNs are used.)

Before a CNA works, documentation of current Florida CNA certification (or a current out-of-state certificate). Before a home health aide works, documentation of at least 40 hours of training or a passed competency test. Training subjects: 1. communication skills; 2. observation, reporting and documentation; 3. reading and recording temperature, pulse and respiration; 4. basic infection control; 5. basic body functions to be reported to the RN supervisor; 6. maintenance of a clean and safe environment; 7. recognition of emergencies and follow-up; 8. physical, emotional and developmental characteristics of populations served, including respect for the patient or client, privacy and property; 9. personal hygiene and grooming techniques; 10. safe transfer techniques and ambulation; 11. normal range of motion and positioning; 12. nutrition and fluid intake; 13. cultural differences in families; 14. food preparation and household chores; 15. assistance with self-administered medication (minimum 2 hours of training, including verification that the aide can read the prescription label); 16. other pertinent topics.

Home health aide training must be performed by or under the general supervision of an RN with at least two years of nursing experience, one of them in home health care. An agency may instead administer the Home Health Aide Competency Test (AHCA 3110-1007) and must keep documentation of the aide's passing result. The practical portion must be administered and evaluated by an RN, or by an LPN under RN supervision.
Home health aides and CNAs must receive in-service training each calendar year and maintain current CPR certification from an approved provider.

Home health aide and CNA responsibilities include: 1. personal care activities in a written assignment by a licensed health professional; 2. maintenance of a clean, safe and healthy environment; 3. other activities taught by a licensed professional for a specific patient, limited to the listed tasks (a–l); 4. keeping records of personal health care activities; 5. observing and reporting appearance and gross behavioral changes to the RN; 6. supervision of self-administered medication, limited to the four listed steps.

Self-administered medication assistance: an RN review and reconciliation of all prescribed and over-the-counter medications, to confirm the patient is medically stable with routine scheduled medications. A licensed health care professional must inform the patient or caregiver of the arrangement and obtain written consent under s. 400.488(2), F.S. Permitted aide actions are listed in (5)(o)1-4.

Responsibilities the home health aide and CNA may not perform (the list starts at 1. therapeutic services requiring licensure and runs through at least 10). The fetched page was cut off partway through this list, so retrieve the full text from the rule.

Each home health agency shall have written policies and procedures that delineate the agency's position with respect to state law and rules on advance directives. The policies shall not condition treatment or admission on whether the individual has executed or waived an advance directive. Conflicts between the agency's policies and a patient's advance directive are handled under Chapter 765, F.S.

The advance-directive policy must include giving each adult patient, before services begin, a copy of 'Health Care Advance Directives – The Patients' Right to Decide' (AHCA, rev. April 2006) or an equivalent written description of Florida law.
The advance-directive policy must include giving each adult patient, before services begin, written information about the agency's policies respecting advance directives.

The advance-directive policy must include the requirement that the patient's medical record document whether or not an advance directive has been executed. A copy of any executed directive goes in the record. If no copy is received, the agency documents that it requested one.
DNRO: cardiopulmonary resuscitation may be withheld or withdrawn only if a valid Do Not Resuscitate Order is present, executed under s. 401.45, F.S. (Department of Health form; rule 64J-2.018).

Acceptance of patients or clients: there must be a reasonable expectation that services can be provided safely in the patient's residence. This includes the ability to communicate with the patient (or the patient's designee) through a same-language staff person or interpreter, or through translation technology. The agency must assure the patient receives services as defined in the plan of care or written agreement, including all assigned visits.

At the start of services, a written agreement between the agency and the patient, client or legal representative, including the information in s. 400.487(1), F.S. It must be signed and dated by an agency representative and the patient, client or representative. A copy goes to the patient or client and the original goes in the file.

For homemaker/companion clients and for home health aide clients who do not need a practitioner's treatment order, the written agreement serves as the service provision plan under s. 400.491(2), F.S. It is kept for one year after services end.

Termination of services for patients or clients needing continuing care: develop a plan and make a referral to another agency or provider before termination. Give written notice of the termination date, the reason (s. 400.491, F.S.) and the plan for continued services. This does not apply to patients paying privately who default through non-payment. The agency should provide social work assistance to help determine eligibility for government-funded programs.

A written comprehensive emergency management plan, prepared and maintained under s. 400.492, F.S., following the criteria in the CEMP (AHCA Form 3110-1022, Rev. March 2013), which is used as the plan format. The plan describes how the agency establishes and maintains an effective response to emergencies and disasters.
The completed plan is forwarded electronically for approval to the contact designated by the Department of Health. The agency reviews the plan annually and makes substantive changes.

Changes in telephone numbers of staff coordinating emergency response (including after-hours numbers) must be reported to the county Emergency Management office and the county health department. A new owner reviews the plan after a change of ownership.

In an emergency, all staff designated for emergency measures must be informed of their duties. If telephone service is unavailable, the agency must have a communication contingency plan (for example cell phones, ham radio, public announcements, driving to the home, or contacting police or rescue services).

On admission, inform patients and caregivers of the county special needs registry (s. 252.355, F.S.). Document in the patient file whether the patient will evacuate or stay, whether the caregiver can take over services, and whether the agency must continue services. For ALF or adult family care home residents, find out the facility's evacuation plan and document it.

On imminent threat of an emergency, contact patients needing ongoing services (and the ALFs and adult family care homes served) to confirm each patient's plan. Before an emergency, establish procedures stating to what extent the agency will continue care during and after it. Ascertain which patients staying home need agency care, and designate staff to continue services.

If the agency ceases operation during an emergency, it must inform affected patients, notify the ALFs and adult family care homes served, and make arrangements for nursing personnel to continue essential services. It must report its status to the local emergency operations center. When unable to continue services to special needs patients, the record must document the efforts made to comply with the plan.

Collect registration information for special needs patients who need continuing care in a disaster and submit it to the county Emergency Management office. Educate registered patients that special needs shelters are an option of last resort and that services may not equal those received at home.

Maintain a current prioritized patient list with the information in s. 400.492(2), F.S., and furnish it to the county health department and Emergency Management office on request. The record of each special needs patient must include the s. 400.492(1) information. The agency must keep in the special needs patient's home a list of patient-specific medications, supplies and equipment (names, dose, frequency, route, time, allergies, physician, pharmacy).

Homemaker/companion registration: the application must state the specific geographic area to be served. Providers holding a registration as of July 1, 2015 may keep serving the counties listed on it if a plan for supervision of staff working outside the primary geographic service area is documented.

Confidential client record (homemaker/companion providers): (a) client's full legal name, address, phone, age, and disability if it is the basis for service; (b) name and phone of the emergency contact, next of kin or legal guardian, and physician; (c) copy of any contract or written service agreement; (d) services provided, with duration and frequency of visits; (e) dietary restrictions, if the provider prepares, orders or accompanies the client to meals; (f) food allergies; (g) activity limitations pertaining to service delivery; (h) copy of any written termination notice.

On accepting a client, there must be a reasonable expectation that the requested services can be provided adequately and safely in the residence. The provider must obtain all needed service-delivery information and supply employees or independent contractors capable of delivering the contracted services, including all visits.

official.notes: I did not find a single AHCA policy checklist or plan-of-operation form for Florida personal care. The required_items list is therefore built from the Chapter 59A-8, F.A.C. sections that require written policies, plans or procedures. Item numbering follows the rule text. Florida licenses the agency on AHCA Form 3110-1011 (HHA) or Form 3110-1003 (homemaker/companion), and AHCA surveys compliance. The survey tool is AHCA's ASPEN 'Home Health Agencies' regulation set, which I located but did not review. The CEMP (AHCA Form 3110-1022) is the mandated format for the emergency plan, and DOH reviews it. Items marked conditional apply only to skilled agencies, to agencies that provide nursing or PT services, or to agencies with satellite offices or LPNs. A non-skilled agency is not required to have a director of nursing under 59A-8.0095(2)(i). A reviewer would expect one organized policy manual, plus the CEMP, the aide training and competency documentation, a sample service agreement, and a sample client record. A non-skilled agency must show RN supervision arrangements and RN supervisory visits. Not reviewed or fetched (check before relying on this list): 59A-8.0215 (Plan of Care), 59A-8.0216 (RN delegation), 59A-8.0219 (medication administration), 59A-8.022 (clinical records), s. 400.487 and s. 400.491 F.S., s. 400.509 F.S., s. 400.4785/430.5025 F.S. dementia training, and the licensure application and addendum forms. The Cornell LII copies are unofficial, and the official text is on flrules.org (Florida Administrative Code). Excluded as application paperwork: forms, fees, financials, background screening and insurance.
